content:
Fox News served up some unwelcome Thanksgiving news on Wednesday as Donald Trump continues to grapple with inflation and the affordability crisis.

“Special Report” anchor Bret Baier dedicated a segment of his show to breaking down the rising cost of the traditional holiday meal.

“You have probably noticed that you’re paying more this Thanksgiving for your holiday meal,” Baier began, noting how “it’s costing about 6% more to feed your family this Turkey Day compared to a year ago, ending three straight years of price drops.”

Fox Business correspondent Kelly Saberi, citing data from the American Farm Bureau Federation, identified the turkey as the biggest driver, with prices jumping 10% year over year.

Watch the segment here:

“We have a couple of reasons to blame,” she explained. “First of all, across the board, everything on the table, diesel and labor shortages are going to affect these prices. But with the bird, they’ve been facing three years of disease, and now they’re catching up in the turkey industry. Also, there is a lot of demand for lean meat.”

Milk prices have climbed 8.6%, which Saberi attributed to “the protein craze, we know everybody wants to get more and more protein in.”

Stuffing, sweet potatoes and cranberries are all more expensive, too.

One small consolation? The price of frozen pie crusts has dropped 2.7%.

Baier deadpan responded: “We can’t just have pie. I mean, you have to have the other stuff.”

He then asked how the cost of this year’s feast stacked up against previous years. Saberi said the price “for this 10-person family that the Farm Bureau looks at” is “up 6% since last year, which seems like a lot,” but when “adjusted for inflation it is 2%.”

“They say the average for all the things on the table, which doesn’t include mashed potatoes I should note for people at home, will be about $56,” she added.

That’s below what Saberi said was the “record high” of $64 in 2022, on the back of the coronavirus pandemic, when then-President Joe Biden was in office, but still considerably above the $48 it would have cost in 2019, during Trump’s first term, pre-COVID, pre-Russia’s war on Ukraine and pre-Trump’s war on Iran.
